sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
During the Lunch 20 promo, lunch brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than the same four weeks last year. That's $34,611 against $32,860, a lift of roughly 5.3%.

The promo window is August 3–30, 2026, compared with August 3–30, 2025. Both cover lunch (11:00–13:59 local) on in-store and Square Online orders, completed only [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion; Definitions §2, Lunch]. Net sales means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

- **2026 promo window:** 1,414 orders, $40,261 gross, $5,373 in discounts and $277 refunded.
- **2025 same window:** 1,194 orders, $34,990 gross, $1,497 in discounts and $633 refunded.

Gross sales rose by about $5,272, but most of that gain went back out as discounts. That's why the net lift is much smaller.

sql-02.question: How many new customers did Lunch 20 bring in?
sql-02.answer:
Lunch 20 brought in 262 new customers. I counted identified customers whose first completed order ever was a Lunch 20 order. That means a completed order with the Lunch 20 discount, placed from August 3 to August 30, 2026, between 11:00 and 13:59 local time, in store or on Square Online [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion; Definitions §2, Lunch].

There were also 331 Lunch 20 orders with no customer attached. I can't tell whether those guests were new, so they aren't in the 262.

sql-03.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
sql-03.answer: We lost 177 regulars over the summer. That uses your definition: a regular has three or more completed orders in March, April and May 2026 and hasn't ordered since the end of August, so no completed order from September 1 on [Definitions §4, Regulars]. sql-04.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
sql-04.answer:
Pickled Vegetables earns the least per unit among sides on Uber Eats delivery. It makes about $1.55 per unit.

This covers completed Uber Eats delivery orders in the Sides category, across all the data we have. The average price paid was $3.11. Uber takes 30% on delivery, which leaves about $2.18. Food cost is $0.63, so about $1.55 remains [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. It sold 193 units.

Fried Egg is next lowest at about $1.61 per unit. Extra Noodles and Steamed Rice both come in near $1.89.

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026 we kept about $2.49 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. The average net payout was about $30.06 for in-store orders and about $27.57 for DoorDash delivery orders.

- **Scope:** Completed orders only, September 1 to 30, 2026. That covers 2,643 in-store orders and 1,271 DoorDash delivery orders. DoorDash pickup orders are left out.
- **In store:** Gross sales minus discounts minus the card processing fee.
- **DoorDash delivery:** Gross sales minus discounts minus the 25% delivery commission on the menu subtotal [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing].
- **Date boundaries:** I used September's start and end in the restaurant's local time zone, but I didn't check how the query handled the boundaries. The figures could be slightly off for orders placed near midnight on the first or last day.

sql-06.question: What was our average tip in September 2026?
sql-06.answer:
Our average tip in September 2026 was $4.95. That covers completed orders from September 1 to 30, using local time.

Only 2,190 of the 7,985 completed orders reported a tip, so the average uses those 2,190. The other orders have no tip recorded, which usually means the channel doesn't pass tips through. I left them out instead of counting them as $0.

sql-07.question: What did we net from DoorDash delivery orders in September 2026 after their commission?
sql-07.answer:
In September 2026 (local time), DoorDash delivery orders netted about $34,862.65 after commission. This covers completed orders only.

- **Orders:** 1,269.
- **Gross sales:** $49,935.79.
- **Discounts:** $2,589.19.
- **Commission:** about $12,483.95, which is 25% of gross sales. That is DoorDash's delivery rate [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing].
- **Net:** gross minus discounts minus commission, which comes to $34,862.65.

Marketplace orders don't carry a processing fee, so none is deducted. I applied the 25% to gross sales before discounts, as the vendor definition says. The terms describe it as a share of the menu subtotal. If DoorDash charges it after discounts, the commission would be lower.

sql-08.question: Since the Seasonal Specials came back on September 1, which drink category has lost the most sales compared with the four weeks before?
sql-08.answer:
House Favorites lost the most. It sold $8,377.25 in the four weeks from Sept 1 to Sept 28, 2026. In the four weeks before, Aug 4 to Aug 31, it sold $9,097.25. That is a drop of $720.00.

pol-01.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
pol-01.answer:
Not on her own authority. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. A $40 comp is above that limit, so it needs the owner's approval. The owner can be reached by text during service [House Policy §2, Comps].

Two other rules apply. Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount. Total comps in a week should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, you review every comp from that week [House Policy §2, Comps].

She could comp up to $25 herself and get your approval for the rest. Or she could text you for approval of the full $40. I haven't proposed anything yet. If you give me the order, I can propose the comp for your approval.

pol-03.answer:

- Marketing texts are capped at four per customer per calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency].
- A discount can't exceed 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve it. The offer must also state an expiry date no more than 14 days out and say "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

pol-11.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
pol-11.answer:
Not as written. I proposed the campaign, but the check blocked it because 20% is over the 15% cap. Nothing has been sent. [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages] says a text discount can't exceed 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves it.

You also can't text the whole list. [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts] allows marketing texts only to customers with verified SMS consent. Anyone who has unsubscribed is excluded. Today that is 943 customers. Customers who only gave us their number when ordering don't count.

Other rules for the message:
- **Expiry:** it must expire within 14 days and say "one per customer" [§5].
- **Wording:** it must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [§6, Required Wording].
- **Timing:** it can't go out between 8pm and 9am [§3, Quiet Hours].

My draft says "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 20% off your next order, one per customer. Offer expires 2026-11-04. Reply STOP to opt out".

You have two options. You can approve the 20% yourself as the owner, which the policy allows. Or I can redraft it at 15% or less, which should pass the check.

pro-06.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
pro-06.answer:
I've drafted the campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's waiting for your approval, and it won't go to everyone with a phone number.

Of 29,762 customers with a phone number, only 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. About 17,135 more gave us a number but never opted in. Policy allows only transactional texts to them, not marketing [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. 848 customers with a phone number have unsubscribed and can't be texted at all.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend, through Sunday Oct 25. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out."

- **Discount and wording:** The 10% is under the 15% cap. The text has an expiry date, "one per customer," the restaurant name and the opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages; §6, Required Wording].
- **Approval needed:** The system's checks passed. Because 563 is over the 500-person cap, you have to approve it personally.
- **Send time:** It has to go out between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

pro-07.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
pro-07.answer:
I can't set up that text. The policy says "Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The 25% is also over the 20% cap that applies without your approval, so it would need your sign-off even on other items.

I haven't drafted or proposed a campaign. Here are two versions I could put together for approval:

- **A different item or category:** the discount would be 20% or less, expire within 7 days, and apply once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5].
- **A Seasonal Specials message with no discount:** it would announce the items without an offer.

Either version would go to regulars, meaning customers with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. Each person would also need to meet the consent rules:

- They have ordered in the last 90 days and have a phone number on file. Otherwise they need verified SMS consent [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts].
- They have not unsubscribed.
- They have not already received the monthly limit of marketing texts [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency].
- The text goes out between 8am and 9pm Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

Tell me which version you want and I'll draft it.

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
Lunch net sales rose by $1,751.36 during Lunch 20 compared with the same dates last year. This covers in-store and Square Online orders only, from 11:00 to 13:59 local time. Net sales means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

- **Lunch 20 window (Aug 3–30, 2026):** net sales were $34,610.93 from 1,414 completed orders. Gross sales were $40,261.46, less $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 in refunds.
- **Same dates in 2025 (Aug 3–30):** net sales were $32,859.57 from 1,194 completed orders. Gross sales were $34,989.77, less $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 in refunds.

That is about 5.3% more net, or 18% more orders. Gross sales rose by $5,271.69, but most of that went back out as promo discounts.

I used the same calendar dates for last year. Aug 3, 2025 fell on a Sunday and Aug 3, 2026 on a Monday, so the weekday mix differs slightly.

Policy basis: [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] and [Definitions §2, Lunch].

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026, we kept about $2.49 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. That is about $30.06 per in-store order against about $27.57 per DoorDash delivery order.

- **Scope:** The figures cover completed orders only. That is 2,643 in-store orders and 1,271 DoorDash delivery orders. DoorDash pickup orders are left out.
- **In-store payout:** Gross sales minus discounts minus the card processing fee.
- **DoorDash payout:** Gross sales minus discounts minus the 25% delivery commission [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. Marketplace unit prices already include the markup over in-store prices [Definitions §5, Marketplaces].
- **Caveat:** The September date range may be off by a few hours at the month boundaries, because the time zone conversion may not match the restaurant's local time exactly. I don't expect that to change the per-order averages much.

pol-01.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
pol-01.answer:
No, not on her own. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. A $40 comp is above that, so the owner has to approve it [House Policy §2, Comps]. The policy says the owner can be reached by text during service.

I've proposed a notification to the owner for the $40 comp. It's pending, and nothing has happened yet.

Two other limits apply. Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount. Total comps for the week should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales.

pol-11.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
pol-11.answer:
Not as written. I proposed the campaign, and the policy check blocked it. Nothing has been sent.

The blocking reason is the discount size. Texted offers are capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves a larger one [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. A 20% offer is over that cap.

You also can't text the whole list. Only customers with verified SMS consent who haven't unsubscribed can get marketing texts. Implied consent, such as giving a phone number when ordering, isn't enough [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. That leaves 943 of your 48,179 customers.

The draft message is: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 20% off your next order, one per customer. Offer expires Nov 5, 2026. Reply STOP to opt out". It names the restaurant, says "one per customer" and ends with the opt-out wording. The expiry is within 14 days [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages; §6, Required Wording]. It would also need to go out between 9am and 8pm local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

You have two options. You can lower the offer to 15% or less, which should pass the check. Or you can approve the 20% yourself as owner, and I can resubmit it on that basis.

ans-01.question: Hi, what can you help me with?
ans-01.answer:
I can answer questions about your restaurant's sales data and your written policies, and I can propose actions for you to approve.

For sales data, I can look at things like:
- Sales, orders, and average tips by day, hour, or channel (in store, Square Online, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub).
- Item sales and margins.
- Customers: new, lost, and regulars.
- Payments, processing fees, commissions, and net payouts.
- Comparisons, such as before and after a date, or this year against last year.

For policies, I can look up your rules on comps, refunds, discounts, and catering. I can also look up marketplace terms on disputes and commissions, and messaging rules on consent, quiet hours, and offers.

I can also propose actions, such as filing a marketplace dispute, comping an order, running a text campaign, or notifying you. Nothing happens until a person approves it, and I can't send, schedule, change, or delete anything myself.

Try asking something like "What were net sales by channel last month?" or "Which items had the best margin on DoorDash this quarter?"

pro-02.question: Text everyone who ordered this month 25% off, tomorrow at 9am.
pro-02.answer:
I proposed the campaign, but the policy check blocked it, so nothing will go out. The 25% discount is over the 20% limit for texted offers unless the owner approves it [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

- **Audience:** 916 customers have a completed order in October (Oct 1–24, local time). Only 214 of them have a phone number on file and haven't unsubscribed, so the proposal targets those 214. Customers with recent orders and a phone number can get marketing texts without a separate opt-in, up to two a month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. I can't see how many texts each person has already had this month, so that limit isn't checked. 214 is under the 300-customer cap [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].
- **Timing:** I can't schedule or send anything. A person has to approve the proposal first. A 9am text is outside quiet hours (9pm to 8am Mountain) [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].
- **Draft message:** "Thanks for ordering with us this month! Enjoy 25% off your next order, one use per customer, valid through Nov 1. Reply STOP to opt out." The offer expires within 7 days and is limited to one use per customer, as the policy requires [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

To get this out, you can either approve 25% as the owner or change the offer to 20% or less. I can re-propose it at 20% if you want.

pro-03.question: Text our recent customers 10% off pastries tomorrow at 9am.

I've drafted the text campaign, but nothing has been sent or scheduled. It's waiting for your approval, and I can't set the 9am send time myself.

- **Audience:** Your policies don't define "recent", so I used customers who ordered in the last 90 days, have a phone number and haven't unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. My count was 586. The system's check counted 575, and that's the number on the proposal.
- **Approval needed:** A campaign over 300 customers needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].
- **Offer:** 10% is under the 20% cap, and the offer is valid only on Oct 25, within the 7-day limit [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. 9am is outside quiet hours, which run 9pm to 8am Mountain [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].
- **Message:** "Good morning! Today only, enjoy 10% off any pastry at our shop. Just mention this text when you order. Offer valid Oct 25 only, one use per customer. Text STOP to stop"
- **Redraft:** My first draft was blocked because it didn't end with the required "Text STOP to stop". I fixed that and the resubmitted draft passed the checks.

I didn't check whether any of these customers have already had two marketing texts this month, which is the limit in §2.

pro-06.answer:
I've proposed the text campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's waiting for your approval.

- **Monthly limit:** Customers can get at most four marketing texts a month [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency]. I didn't check how many each of these 563 has already had this month.

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
Lunch brought in about $1,751 more in net sales during Lunch 20 than in the same four weeks last year. Lunch 20 ran August 3–30, 2026, and I compared it with August 3–30, 2025. Both periods cover lunch (11:00–13:59 local time) in store and on Square Online [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion; Definitions §2, Lunch].

- **2026 promo window:** net sales were $34,610.93 on 1,414 completed orders.
- **2025 same dates:** net sales were $32,859.57 on 1,194 completed orders.
- **Net sales:** these are gross sales minus discounts and refunds.

Gross sales (before discounts) rose more, by $5,271.69, from $34,989.77 to $40,261.46. Discounts rose from $1,497.21 to $5,373.26, and that cost took most of the gross gain. So the promo drew more orders, but it kept little of the added revenue.

sql-04.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
sql-04.answer:
Pickled Vegetables earns the least per unit among the Sides on Uber Eats delivery, at about $1.55 each. I counted all completed Uber Eats delivery orders and used the items in the Sides category. The query didn't filter by date, so it covers all of them.

Pickled Vegetables sells at $3.11 on Uber Eats. Uber takes 30% on delivery, about $0.93 [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. Food cost is $0.63, which leaves roughly $1.55. Across the period, 193 units sold.

Fried Egg is close behind at about $1.61 per unit. The other sides earn more:
- Extra Noodles: about $1.89.
- Steamed Rice: about $1.90.
- Extra Broth: about $2.51.
- Extra Meat: about $3.22.

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026, we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. The average net payout was $30.11 per in-store order (2,633 orders) and $27.47 per DoorDash delivery order (1,269 orders). That is $3,011.31 against $2,747.25 in cents, a gap of $264.05 per 100 orders.

This covers completed orders only. Net payout is gross sales minus discounts, then minus one more deduction depending on the channel:

- **In store:** the payment processing fee, using completed payments.
- **DoorDash delivery:** the 25% commission on gross sales [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. DoorDash orders don't carry a processing fee in this calculation.

DoorDash prices already include the 25% markup, so the unit price on those orders is higher than in store [Definitions §5, Marketplaces]. That markup is why the gap is smaller than the commission alone would suggest.

| Pumpkin Spice Latte | 1,288 | $6,414.24 |

pol-01.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
pol-01.answer:
No, not on her own. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket for a food-quality or long-wait complaint. A $40 comp is above that, so it needs the owner (Linh), who can be reached by text during service [House Policy §2, Comps]. Your manager could comp up to $25 herself, or get Linh's approval for the full $40.

I've proposed a notification to Linh about the $40 comp. The proposal is pending, and nothing has been sent or comped yet. The check returned no issues.

Total comps for the week should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, Linh reviews every comp from it [House Policy §2, Comps].

pol-03.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
pol-03.answer:
No. Under [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], no text of any kind can go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time. A 10pm send falls inside that window, so it would break the rule.

Send the promotion between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time instead. Other rules also apply:
- Only customers with verified SMS consent can get it [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].
- Each customer can get at most four marketing texts a month [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency].
- Any discount in the text must stay within the limits in [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I can't send or schedule texts myself. I can propose a campaign for you to approve if you'd like one.

pol-04.question: A customer wants to cancel a catering order three days before pickup. Do they get the deposit back?
pol-04.answer:
Yes. Cancelling three days (72 hours) before pickup is earlier than the 48-hour cutoff, so the deposit is refundable. [House Policy §6, Catering] says the deposit is refundable up to 48 hours before pickup and is kept after that.

If the cancellation comes in less than 48 hours before pickup, the restaurant keeps the deposit. The deposit is 50% of the order. Catering orders over $300 also need the owner's confirmation.

I didn't look up this customer's order, so I haven't confirmed the pickup time or the deposit amount.

pol-11.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?

Texts can only go out between 9am and 8pm [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

pro-02.answer:
I proposed the campaign, but the check blocked it, and nothing has been scheduled or sent.

Of the 846 customers who ordered between Oct 1 and Oct 24, only 200 have a phone number and haven't unsubscribed. They qualify as recent customers [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. 200 is under the 300-customer cap [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size]. 9am is outside quiet hours [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

My draft says: "Thanks for ordering with us this month! Enjoy 25% off your next order, one use per customer, valid through Oct 31. Excludes Seasonal Specials. Reply STOP to opt out."

I didn't check how many marketing texts each customer has already had this month. The limit is two per calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts].

You can either approve 25% as an exception or have me re-propose at 20%. A person still has to approve it either way.

pro-07.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
pro-07.answer:
I can't set up this text. Our messaging policy says "Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The same section caps any discount in a text at 20% unless you approve it, so 25% would also need your approval. Because of the first rule, your approval wouldn't change the outcome for Seasonal Specials.

Here are some options that fit the rules:
- **Different items:** I can draft a text for regulars with up to 20% off items other than Seasonal Specials. The offer must expire within 7 days and apply once per customer. If you want more than 20%, you would have to approve it.
- **Seasonal Specials without a discount:** I can draft a text announcing them, with no offer in it.

Either way, I'd count regulars as customers with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. I'd send only to those who ordered in the last 90 days and have a phone number, or who have verified SMS consent. I'd leave out anyone who has unsubscribed. Texts can't go out between 9pm and 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; §3, Quiet Hours].

Tell me which option you want and I'll size the audience and write the message.

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
During the Lunch 20 promo, lunch brought in about $1,751.36 more in net sales than it did in the same weeks last year. Net sales here means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

I compared August 3 to 30, 2026 with August 3 to 30, 2025. Both periods cover lunch only (11:00 to 13:59 local time), on in-store and Square Online orders, and count completed orders only. Those are the promotion's own dates, hours and channels [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] and the lunch hours [Definitions §2, Lunch].

- **2026 promo window:** 1,414 orders, $40,261.46 gross, $5,373.26 in discounts, and $34,610.93 net.
- **2025 same window:** 1,194 orders, $34,989.77 gross, $1,497.21 in discounts, and $32,859.57 net.

Gross sales rose by about $5,271.69, but the 20% discount took back most of that. The gain is therefore much smaller after discounts.

sql-03.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
sql-03.answer:
We lost 177 regulars over the summer. Of the 599 identified customers who qualified as regulars in spring, 177 have not ordered since the end of August.

The owner's definition is a customer with three or more completed orders in March, April and May 2026 who has not ordered since the end of August [Definitions §4, Regulars]. Summer there means June, July and August. I counted a customer as lost if they have no completed order from 1 September 2026 through today, 24 October. Unidentified guest orders can't be tied to a customer, so they aren't in either number.

sql-04.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
sql-04.answer:
Pickled Vegetables earns the least per unit among the Sides on Uber Eats delivery, about $1.55 each. This covers completed Uber Eats delivery orders and the six items in the Sides category. I didn't limit it to a date range, so it counts all of that history.

The average price paid on Uber Eats was $3.11. Uber's 30% delivery commission takes about $0.93 of that [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. Food cost is $0.63. That leaves roughly $1.55 per unit, and 193 units were sold.

Fried Egg is next lowest at about $1.61 per unit. The other four sides earn between about $1.89 and $3.22.

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026, we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. That's $30.11 against $27.47.

The figures cover completed orders only. In store is 2,633 orders and DoorDash delivery is 1,269 orders. "Kept" means net payout: gross sales minus discounts, then minus the card processing fee for in-store orders or DoorDash's commission for DoorDash orders.

DoorDash takes 25% of the menu subtotal on delivery orders [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing], so I applied 25% of each order's gross sales. DoorDash prices already include the markup over in-store prices [Definitions §5, Marketplaces], and I used them as recorded.

DoorDash orders are larger on average because of that markup. The gap is small even though the commission is 25%, because the in-store figure only loses the processing fee.

sql-09.question: Which of the Seasonal Specials is worth keeping on the menu all year?
sql-09.answer:

- **Maple Pecan Cold Brew:** $7,183.20 on 1,460 units.
- **Apple Cider Chai:** $6,255.16 on 1,412 units.
- **Peppermint Mocha:** $6,644.40 on 1,356 units.
- **Pumpkin Spice Latte:** $6,414.24 on 1,288 units.

Apple Cider Chai sits second in my list above only because I listed it first. By margin, Peppermint Mocha ($6,644.40) is second, then Pumpkin Spice Latte, then Apple Cider Chai. Maple Pecan Cold Brew leads Peppermint Mocha by about $539.

pol-01.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
pol-01.answer:
No, she can't comp the full $40 on her own. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. Anything above $25 needs the owner's approval, and the owner can be reached by text during service [House Policy §2, Comps].

You have two options. She can comp up to $25 herself. Or she can get your approval for the full $40.

I've proposed a notification to the owner about the $40 comp. It's pending, and nothing has been done yet. Comps should also stay under 1% of the week's gross sales, or you'll review every comp from that week [House Policy §2, Comps].

pol-07.question: A student is redeeming a free loyalty drink and wants their 10% off the rest. Can they have both?
pol-07.answer:
Yes, the student can have both. A free loyalty drink isn't classed as a discount, so it can be combined with a standard discount on the rest of the order. The student gets 10% off with ID. [House Policy §4, Discounts]

Two limits apply:

On $66,116.52 in sales, the 1% limit would be about $661.

Two caveats. I identified comps by a discount name containing "comp", so that may include or miss some. Your week boundaries may also differ from mine. Either way, the week is over 1%, so the owner should review every comp from it.

The same policy caps a manager at $25 per ticket. Anything above that needs the owner. Comps for friends, family or staff aren't allowed at any amount. Those are the things to look for in the review.

pol-11.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
pol-11.answer:
Not as written. I proposed the 20% text, and the policy check blocked it because 20% is over the 15% cap. Nothing has been sent.

Customer Messaging Policy §5 (Offers in Messages) caps a text discount at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves a higher one. The same section says the offer needs an expiry date no more than 14 days out and the words "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

Only customers with verified SMS consent who haven't unsubscribed can get marketing texts. Customers who only gave us a phone number don't count [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. That gives 943 customers on your list.

Texts also can't go out between 8pm and 9am [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours]. Every marketing text must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

I drafted this message: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 20% off your next order! One per customer. Expires 2026-11-03. Reply STOP to opt out"

Your options are to approve 20% as the owner, or to drop to 15% or less. If you tell me to go with 15%, I can propose that version.

pol-12.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?
pol-12.answer:
No. A lead can't approve 25% off, whether or not the customer is a regular and whether or not the order is catering.

- **Discount limit:** A lead can approve a discount above 10%, but any discount above 20% needs the owner (Dana). 25% is over that line. [House Policy §4, Discounts]
- **Regulars:** The policies define a regular as someone with four or more completed orders in a month. That gives regulars no extra discount authority. [Definitions §2, Regulars]
- **Catering:** Catering orders over $300 need the owner's confirmation. Catering also needs 72 hours' notice and a 50% deposit. [House Policy §6, Catering]
- **Seasonal Specials:** These are never discounted, so they would have to come off the discounted order. [House Policy §4, Discounts]

A lead could offer up to 20% on their own authority. Anything higher, such as 25%, has to go to Dana first.

pro-02.question: Text everyone who ordered this month 25% off, tomorrow at 9am.
pro-02.answer:
I drafted the campaign, but the policy check blocked it, so nothing is scheduled or sent. I can't send or schedule texts myself. A person has to approve any campaign.

The check blocked it because 25% is over the 20% limit on discounts in messages. Going higher needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

The other checks are fine:
- **Audience:** 846 customers ordered in October through Oct 24. Only 200 of them have a phone number and haven't unsubscribed. That is under the 300 limit [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].
- **Consent:** All 200 ordered within the last 90 days, so they can get marketing texts without a separate opt-in. The limit is two marketing texts per calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts].
- **Timing:** 9am is outside quiet hours, which run 9pm to 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

The draft message says: "Thanks for ordering with us this month! Show this text for 25% off one order through Oct 31. One use per customer. Reply STOP to opt out."

To get this through, you can approve the 25% yourself, or I can redraft it at 20%.

pro-03.question: Text our recent customers 10% off pastries tomorrow at 9am.
pro-03.answer:
I've drafted the campaign, but nothing has been sent or scheduled. It's waiting for your approval, and I can't set the 9am send time myself.

I took "recent customers" to mean people with a phone number and a completed order in the last 90 days who haven't unsubscribed. Your policies don't define "recent", so that's my assumption based on [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. My own count was 586. The system's check recounted it at 570, and that's the figure to go by.

The audience is over 300, so you have to approve it [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].

The message reads: "Treat yourself! Enjoy 10% off any pastry, one use per customer, valid through Oct 31. Just mention this text when you order. Text STOP to stop".

- **Discount:** 10% is under the 20% cap, and the offer expires within 7 days [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Timing:** 9am is after the 8am end of quiet hours [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].
- **Wording:** My first draft was blocked because the opt-out line didn't match the required wording. I fixed it.

I haven't checked two things. One is whether any of these customers has already had two marketing texts this month, because I have no message log to look at. The other is whether any pastries count as Seasonal Specials, which can't be discounted in a message.

pro-06.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.

I've drafted the campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's waiting for your approval.

Of the 29,762 customers with a phone number, only 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. Another 28,351 gave us a number but never opted in. Policy allows only transactional texts for them, not promotions [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. 848 customers with a phone number have unsubscribed, and they can't be texted at all.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend, through Sunday 10/25. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out"

The system checks passed for the discount, the wording and the audience. 10% is under the 15% cap, and the expiry and "one per customer" wording meet the offer rules [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The message names the restaurant and has the opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording]. Because 563 is over the 500-person cap, you have to approve it yourself. It also has to go out between 9am and 8pm local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

pro-07.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
pro-07.answer:
I can't set up that text. Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message, so a 25% offer on them isn't allowed. The 25% also goes over the 20% limit that applies without the owner's approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I haven't proposed or sent anything. Here are two versions that would fit the rules:
- **Different items:** a discount of up to 20% on items other than Seasonal Specials. The offer would expire within 7 days and apply once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **No discount:** a message that announces the Seasonal Specials at full price.

Either version would name Ridgeline Coffee and end with "Text STOP to stop" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

A regular is someone with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. Each recipient would also need a phone number and an order in the last 90 days, or verified SMS consent. Nobody who has unsubscribed can be texted. Nothing can go out between 9pm and 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

Tell me which version you want and I'll count the audience and draft the message for approval.

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
During the Lunch 20 promotion, lunch brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than in the same four weeks last year. I'm treating Lunch 20 as the owner's definition: August 3 to 30, 2026, lunch hours, in store and Square Online [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion]. Lunch is 11:00 to 13:59 local time [Definitions §2, Lunch]. I compared it with August 3 to 30, 2025, using the same hours and channels. Net sales means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds, on completed orders only.

- **2026 promo window:** net sales were $34,610.93 from 1,414 orders. That is $40,261.46 gross, less $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 in refunds.
- **2025 same dates:** net sales were $32,859.57 from 1,194 orders. That is $34,989.77 gross, less $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 in refunds.

Gross sales rose by about $5,272, but the promo discounts ate most of that gain. Orders were up about 18%.

sql-03.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
sql-03.answer:
We lost 177 regulars over the summer of 2026. The owner's definition says a regular has three or more completed orders in three months. Summer is June through August. A regular lost over the summer had three or more completed orders in March, April and May and hasn't ordered since the end of August [Definitions §4, Regulars].

599 identified customers met the regular test in spring (March to May 2026). Of those, 177 have no completed order from September 1 through today, October 24. I counted only completed orders from identified customers, because guest orders with no customer ID can't be tied to a person.

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026, we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. The average was $30.11 per in-store order and $27.47 per DoorDash delivery order.

These figures cover completed orders only. There were 2,633 in-store orders and 1,269 DoorDash delivery orders. "Kept" means net payout:

- **In store:** gross sales minus discounts minus the card processing fee.
- **DoorDash delivery:** gross sales minus discounts minus the 25% delivery commission [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. The commission is applied to the order's gross sales, which is the menu subtotal.

DoorDash pickup orders are left out. They carry a 15% commission instead.

sql-07.question: What did we net from DoorDash delivery orders in September 2026 after their commission?
sql-07.answer:
For September 2026 (local time), completed DoorDash delivery orders came to about $34,862.65 net after commission. That covers 1,269 orders.

Another option is to comp $25 or less, which she can approve herself. Also, total comps in a week should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales [House Policy §2, Comps].

pol-03.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
pol-03.answer:
No. Under [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], no text of any kind may go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time. A 10pm text falls inside that window, so it would break the rule. Send it between 9am and 8pm instead.

Two other rules apply to promotional texts. Only customers with verified SMS consent can receive them [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. Any discount offer is limited to 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve more. It must also carry an expiry date within 14 days and the words "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

pol-11.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
pol-11.answer:
Not as written. I drafted the campaign, but the check blocked it because 20% is over the 15% cap. Nothing has been sent or scheduled.

The policy caps text offers at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve more [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The check did not treat your request as that approval, so the proposal is blocked.

Two things would get it through:
- **Lower the discount.** At 15% or less the offer can go out, as long as the dollar value is also within $10.
- **Approve the 20% yourself.** The check did not accept the 20% in this proposal, so you would need to approve it outside this proposal.

The audience would be 563 customers. These are the customers with verified text consent who haven't unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. Customers who only gave us a phone number are excluded.

The draft message reads: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 20% off your next order, one per customer. Valid through Nov 6, 2026. Reply STOP to opt out." That wording and the expiry meet the offer and wording rules [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording]. The send also has to fall between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

pol-12.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?
pol-12.answer:
No. A lead can't approve 25% off on their own. Any discount above 20% needs the owner [House Policy §4, Discounts]. A lead can approve only discounts above 10% and up to 20%.

Catering adds its own rules. Orders over $300 need the owner's confirmation [House Policy §6, Catering]. Catering also needs 72 hours' notice and a 50% deposit, and it is pickup only. Seasonal Specials are never discounted, so they would have to come off the discounted amount [House Policy §4, Discounts].

The policies don't give "regular" a special discount rate, so being a regular doesn't change these limits. A lead could offer up to 20%. For 25%, the owner has to approve.

pol-13.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?
pol-13.answer:
Nine stamps earn a free drink. You earn one stamp per drink, and only when the customer gives a phone number at checkout [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

The free drink can't be used on a Seasonal Special. The loyalty program excludes Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea. The reward covers any size from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]. The house discount rules also say Seasonal Specials are never discounted [House Policy §4, Discounts].

A free drink reward expires 60 days after it is issued. Stamps expire 12 months after they are earned [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

pol-15.question: What discount do hospital staff get?
pol-15.answer:
The policies don't list a discount for hospital staff. The standard register discounts in [House Policy §4, Discounts] are:

- 10% for students and seniors with ID.
- 15% for first responders in uniform.

Hospital staff aren't named in either group. Any discount above 15% on one order needs a manager, and any discount above 30% needs the owner. Discounts don't combine, and the largest applicable one applies. If you want to offer hospital staff a discount, you would need to set it as a new rule or approve it case by case.

ans-01.question: Hi, what can you help me with?
ans-01.answer:
I can answer questions about your restaurant's sales data and your written policies. I can't change or send anything myself. When something needs doing, I can propose it for a person to approve.

Here's what I can do:

- **Sales and orders:** totals by day, hour, or channel (in store, Square Online, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub), average tips, discounts, and refunds.
- **Items and margins:** top sellers, food cost, and item margin by channel, including marketplace commissions.
- **Customers:** new, lost, and repeat customers, and who can be contacted by text or email.
- **Payouts and fees:** net payout per order, processing fees, and commissions.
- **Policies:** your rules on comps, refunds, discounts, catering, marketplace disputes, and messaging consent. I can also look up how you define terms like lunch or regular.
- **Proposed actions:** a marketplace dispute, a comp, a text campaign with the full message written out, or a note to you as owner. Each one waits for approval before anything happens.

Try a question like "What were net sales last week by channel?" or "Which customers haven't ordered since July?"

Texts can't go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time, so it needs to be sent during the day [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
Lunch brought in $1,751.36 more in net sales during Lunch 20 than in the same period last year. The promotion ran Aug 3 to Aug 30, 2026, and I compared it with Aug 3 to Aug 30, 2025 [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion].

The comparison covers lunch only, 11:00 to 13:59 local time [Definitions §2, Lunch]. It includes completed orders in store and on Square Online, the two channels the promotion covered. Net sales are gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

- **2026:** $34,610.93 net, from 1,414 orders. Gross sales were $40,261.46, discounts were $5,373.26, and refunds were $277.27.
- **2025:** $32,859.57 net, from 1,194 orders. Gross sales were $34,989.77, discounts were $1,497.21, and refunds were $632.99.

Gross sales rose by $5,271.69, but the 20% discount took back most of that. Net sales rose about 5.3%.

sql-03.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
sql-03.answer:
We lost 177 regulars over the summer of 2026.

Your definition is a customer with three or more completed orders in March, April and May who has not ordered since the end of August [Definitions §4, Regulars]. Orders with no customer attached can't be tied to a person, so they aren't in this count.

Some of these customers may have ordered during June to August and stopped only at the end of the summer. The definition allows that, and I didn't separate them out.

sql-04.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
sql-04.answer:
Pickled Vegetables earns the least per unit among side dishes on Uber Eats delivery. It makes about $1.55 per unit.

- **Method:** Uber takes 30% on delivery [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. I took the average Uber Eats unit price of $3.11, kept 70% of it, and subtracted the $0.63 food cost.
- **Close behind:** Fried Egg makes about $1.61 per unit.
- **Next:** Extra Noodles ($1.89) and Steamed Rice ($1.90) are next.
- **Top of the range:** Extra Broth makes $2.51 and Extra Meat $3.22.
- **Volume:** Pickled Vegetables sold 193 units over this period.

House Favorites lost the most. Its sales were $9,097.25 in the four weeks before the launch (Aug 4 to Aug 31) and $8,377.25 in the four weeks after (Sep 1 to Sep 28). That is a drop of $720.00.

Matcha was the only other drink category that fell, by $215.00, from $9,232.50 to $9,017.50. Signature Drinks, Bubble Tea and Flights all rose slightly. Seasonal Specials went from $0 to $9,712.00, because it wasn't on the menu before September 1.

I've proposed a notification to the owner about the $40 comp. It's pending, and nothing has been approved or done yet. Two other things to know:
- The manager could comp up to $25 herself.
- Total comps for the week should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales [House Policy §2, Comps].

pol-03.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
pol-03.answer:
No. Under [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], no text of any kind can go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time. A text at 10pm falls inside that window. Send it between 9am and 8pm instead.

Promotional texts also have other rules:
- They can only go to customers with verified SMS consent, and never to anyone who has unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].
- Any discount is capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve more. The text must also state an expiry date no more than 14 days out and say "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- The text must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

The policy says the deposit "is refundable up to 48 hours before pickup and kept after that" [House Policy §6, Catering]. The customer would lose the deposit only if they cancelled less than 48 hours before pickup.

pol-12.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?
pol-12.answer:
No. A lead can't give 25% off, catering or not. Any discount above 20% needs the owner, who is Dana. [House Policy §4, Discounts] Leads can approve discounts above 10% and up to 20%. The policies don't give regulars a separate discount rate, so being a regular doesn't change this. A regular is someone with four or more completed orders in a month. [Definitions §2, Regulars]

Catering adds two conditions. Any catering order over $300 needs the owner's confirmation. [House Policy §6, Catering] Catering also needs 72 hours' notice and a 50% deposit, and it is pickup only. Seasonal Specials can never be discounted. [House Policy §4, Discounts]

A lead could offer up to 20% on their own authority. For 25%, Dana would have to approve it.

pol-13.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?
pol-13.answer:
Nine stamps earn a free drink. You earn one stamp per drink bought, in store or online, when you give your phone number at checkout [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

The free drink can't be used on a Seasonal Special. Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea are excluded. The reward covers a drink of any size from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]. House policy also says Seasonal Specials are never discounted [House Policy §4, Discounts].

Stamps expire 12 months after they are earned. An issued free drink reward expires after 60 days [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

pol-14.question: A DoorDash customer called us saying their pho arrived cold and wants a refund. Can we refund them?
pol-14.answer:
No, we shouldn't refund this one ourselves. Cold food on a DoorDash order is covered by [Marketplace Terms §4, Late, Cold, or Damaged Deliveries]. Delays and damage after the courier picks up the order are the platform's cost, not ours. If a customer complains to us about a cold delivery, we refer them to DoorDash support. We don't issue a refund or a credit from our side. The Grubhub exception for orders we marked ready too early doesn't apply to DoorDash.

I didn't look up the specific order. Tell the customer to contact DoorDash support about the refund.

pol-15.question: What discount do hospital staff get?
pol-15.answer:
The policies don't list a discount for hospital staff. [House Policy §4, Discounts] sets only these standard discounts:

- 10% for students and seniors with ID.
- 15% for first responders in uniform.

Hospital staff aren't named, so they don't get a standard register discount. Any discount above 15% on one order needs a manager. Any discount above 30% needs the owner. Discounts aren't combined, and the largest applicable one applies. If you want to offer hospital staff a discount, it would have to be a new rule or a one-off approval.

ans-01.question: Hi, what can you help me with?
ans-01.answer:
I can answer questions about your restaurant's sales data and your written policies. I can also propose actions for you to approve. I can't carry out any action myself.

For sales data, I can look at:
- Sales, orders, and items, including margins and food cost.
- Customers, such as new, lost, and regular customers.
- Payments, tips, and fees.
- Channels, meaning in-store, Square Online, DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub, including commissions and net payouts.
- Comparisons, such as before and after a date, or this year against last year.

For your policies, I can look up the rules on comps, refunds, discounts, catering, marketplace disputes, and texting customers. That covers consent, quiet hours, and who has to approve something.

I can also propose a marketplace dispute, a comp, a text campaign with the full message written out, or a note to the owner. Nothing happens until a person approves it.

Try a question like "What were net sales by channel last month?" or "Which items had the best margin on DoorDash in September?"

pro-02.question: Text everyone who ordered this month 25% off, tomorrow at 9am.
pro-02.answer:
I drafted the campaign, but the policy check blocked it, so nothing is queued. The check failed because 25% is over the 20% cap on discounts in messages. That cap can only be exceeded with the owner's approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I also can't schedule or send texts myself. A person has to approve the campaign first.

- **Audience:** 200 customers. They had a completed order from Oct 1 to Oct 24, 2026, have a phone number on file, and haven't unsubscribed. They ordered within the last 90 days, so they can get marketing texts without a separate opt-in. Each person can get at most two marketing texts this calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. 200 is under the 300-customer limit [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].
- **Who is left out:**
  - 646 identified customers have no phone on file.
  - 8 have unsubscribed.
  - 3,623 orders had no customer attached, so I can't text those guests.
- **Timing:** 9am is outside quiet hours, which run 9pm to 8am Mountain time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].
- **Offer terms:** Offers must expire within 7 days and apply once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Draft message:** "Ridgeline Coffee: thanks for stopping by this month! Enjoy 25% off your next order, one use per customer, valid through 2026-10-31. Text STOP to stop." The wording follows [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

To get this through, you can approve the 25% as an owner exception, or I can redraft it at 20% or less.

pro-06.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
pro-06.answer:

Of the 29,762 customers with a phone number, I limited the audience to those with verified SMS consent who haven't unsubscribed. Policy only allows marketing texts to them, so a phone number alone doesn't qualify [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].

If you approve, the audience may be the full 563, not the 121 I intended.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: 10% off any pho this weekend! Valid through Sunday, Oct 25, 2026. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out". The 10% is under the 15% cap, and the draft has an expiry date and "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. pro-07.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
pro-07.answer:
I can't set up this text. The messaging policy rules out both parts of it.

- **Seasonal Specials:** They "may never be discounted in a message" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **25% discount:** Any discount in a text over 20% needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I haven't proposed the campaign or pulled an audience count.

Here are two versions that would fit the rules:
- **Different items:** Offer up to 20% off items other than Seasonal Specials. The offer has to expire within 7 days and apply once per customer.
- **Loyalty message:** Send a stamp-balance or free-drink reminder with no offer in it.

Either way, "regulars" means customers with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. For a marketing text, they also need an order in the last 90 days and a phone number on file, or verified SMS consent. Anyone who has unsubscribed gets nothing. Customers on the existing-relationship basis can get at most two marketing texts a month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts; Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency].

Do you want me to draft one of these and propose it for approval?

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
During the Lunch 20 promo, lunch brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than the same four weeks last year. I compared August 3–30, 2026 with August 3–30, 2025. Both periods cover lunch (11:00–13:59 local) on in-store and Square Online orders only, which is how your policy defines the promotion's window and its comparison [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] [Definitions §2, Lunch]. I counted completed orders only.

- **Net sales:** $34,610.93 this year against $32,859.57 last year. Net is gross sales minus discounts and refunds.
- **Gross sales before discounts:** $40,261.46 against $34,989.77, which is $5,271.69 more.
- **Discounts:** $5,373.26 this year against $1,497.21 last year. The 20% discount took back most of the gross gain.
- **Orders:** 1,414 against 1,194.

I matched calendar dates, not weekdays. August 3 was a Sunday last year and a Monday this year.

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026 we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. The average net payout was $30.11 for in-store orders and $27.47 for DoorDash delivery orders. The figures cover completed orders only: 2,633 in store and 1,269 DoorDash delivery.

Net payout is gross sales minus discounts, then minus the payment processing fee for in-store orders or minus commission for DoorDash. DoorDash takes 25% of the menu subtotal on delivery orders [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. DoorDash prices already include the markup of up to 25% over in-store prices [Definitions §5, Marketplaces], so a DoorDash order is usually larger. That larger order is why the gap is small despite the 25% commission.

sql-08.question: Since the Seasonal Specials came back on September 1, which drink category has lost the most sales compared with the four weeks before?
sql-08.answer:
House Favorites lost the most. Its item sales were $8,377.25 in the four weeks after the September 1 launch (Sept 1–28), down from $9,097.25 in the four weeks before (Aug 4–31). That is a drop of $720.00.

sql-09.question: Which of the Seasonal Specials is worth keeping on the menu all year?

pol-03.answer:
No. Under [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], no text of any kind can go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If you don't know a customer's local time, use Central time. 10pm falls inside that window, so a promotional text at that hour isn't allowed. Schedule it between 9am and 8pm in the recipient's local time.

The message must also name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

pol-12.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?
pol-12.answer:
No. A lead can't approve 25% off. Under [House Policy §4, Discounts], a discount above 10% needs a lead, but any discount above 20% needs the owner, who is Dana per [House Policy §1, Scope and Authority]. Being a regular doesn't change that. The policy gives no exception for regulars, so the owner would have to approve it.

Two catering rules also apply under [House Policy §6, Catering]. A catering order over $300 needs the owner's confirmation anyway. Seasonal Specials can never be discounted, so they would have to come off the discounted amount [House Policy §4, Discounts].

A lead could approve up to 20% off, if the order qualifies.

pol-13.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?
pol-13.answer:

House policy also says Seasonal Specials are never discounted [House Policy §4, Discounts].

Stamps expire 12 months after they are earned, and an issued reward expires after 60 days [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

pol-14.question: A DoorDash customer called us saying their pho arrived cold and wants a refund. Can we refund them?
pol-14.answer:
No, we shouldn't refund this one ourselves. Under [Marketplace Terms §4, Late, Cold, or Damaged Deliveries], a cold delivery after the courier picks it up is the platform's cost, not ours. If a customer complains to us about a cold delivery, we refer them to the platform's support. We don't issue a refund or credit from our side.

The only exception is for Grubhub orders where we marked the order ready more than 10 minutes early. This order is from DoorDash, so the exception doesn't apply.

The manager comp allowance in [House Policy §2, Comps] covers up to $25 for food quality complaints. Marketplace Terms §4 is the more specific rule for marketplace deliveries, so I'd tell the customer to contact DoorDash support.

pro-06.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
pro-06.answer:
I proposed the text campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's pending and needs your approval.

Of 29,762 customers with a phone number, only 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. The policy only allows marketing texts to those customers [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. The rest gave a number but never opted in, so they can't get a promotion.

I drafted the message for the 121 consenting customers who ordered in the last 180 days. The system check counted the audience as 563, not 121. That's over the 500-customer limit, so it needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size]. The other 442 haven't ordered in more than 180 days, and campaigns to them need owner approval whatever the size. If you approve it as filed, it may go to all 563, not just the 121.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend, through Sunday Oct 26. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out"

The 10% discount is under the 15% cap, and the message has an expiry date and "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. It names the restaurant and ends with the required opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

pro-07.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
pro-07.answer:
I can't set up this text. Ridgeline Coffee's messaging policy says Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The same section also caps any text discount at 20% unless you approve it, so 25% would need your approval even on other items.

Here is what I could set up instead:
- **Different items:** a text for regulars with up to 20% off non-Seasonal items. Or I could propose 25% on non-Seasonal items for you to approve.
- **Terms:** the offer would expire within 7 days and apply once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Wording:** the message would name Ridgeline Coffee and end with "Text STOP to stop" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].
- **Audience:** a regular has four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. They would also need an order in the last 90 days and a phone number, or verified SMS consent. Anyone who has unsubscribed gets nothing [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts].

If you want that, tell me which items and what discount. I'll count the audience before proposing it.

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
Lunch brought in about $1,395.64 more during Lunch 20 than in the same four weeks last year. That is net sales of $34,888.20 versus $33,492.56, an increase of about 4.2%.

- **Period and filters:** I compared August 3–30, 2026 with August 3–30, 2025. Both cover lunch (11:00–13:59 Chicago time) on in-store and Square Online orders only, completed orders only. That is the promotion's window as your policy defines it [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] [Definitions §2, Lunch].
- **Net sales:** I counted net sales as gross sales minus discounts. I did not subtract refunds, because the refund query timed out.
- **Gross sales:** Gross sales rose from $34,989.77 to $40,261.46, which is $5,271.69 more.
- **Orders:** Orders rose from 1,194 to 1,414.
- **Discounts:** Discounts grew from $1,497.21 to $5,373.26. That is why the net gain is much smaller than the gross gain.

sql-02.question: How many new customers did Lunch 20 bring in?
sql-02.answer:
Lunch 20 brought in 262 new customers. That counts identified customers whose first completed order ever was a Lunch 20 order. A Lunch 20 order is a completed order carrying the discount. There were 811 Lunch 20 orders in total. 331 of them came from unidentified guests with no customer record. I can't tell whether those guests were new, so they aren't in the 262.

sql-03.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
sql-03.answer:
We lost 177 regulars over the summer of 2026. The owner's definition says a regular has three or more completed orders in three months. I counted identified customers with at least 3 completed orders from March 1 to May 31, 2026 and no completed order from September 1 through today, October 24. Orders from guests with no customer ID can't be tied to a person, so they aren't in this count. Completed orders only.

sql-04.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
sql-04.answer:
Pickled Vegetables earns the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, about $1.55 each. That covers all completed Uber Eats delivery orders in the data, for items in the Sides category.

Pickled Vegetables sell at an average of $3.11 on Uber Eats. Uber's 30% delivery commission takes about $0.93 of that, and food cost is $0.63. That leaves roughly $1.55 per unit, and we sold 193 units.

Fried Egg is next lowest at about $1.61 per unit. Extra Noodles and Steamed Rice both come in around $1.90.

The commission rate comes from [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. The prices already include the marketplace markup [Definitions §5, Marketplaces].

sql-08.question: Since the Seasonal Specials came back on September 1, which drink category has lost the most sales compared with the four weeks before?
sql-08.answer:
House Favorites lost the most sales, though the drop was small. I compared the four weeks after the September 1 launch (Sept 1–28) with the four weeks before it (Aug 4–31). The figures are item sales from completed orders, in local time.

- **House Favorites:** down $720, from $9,097.25 to $8,377.25.
- **Matcha:** down $215, from $9,232.50 to $9,017.50.
- **Signature Drinks, Bubble Tea and Flights:** all slightly up.
- **Seasonal Specials:** brought in $9,712 after launch, and had no sales before because they are off the menu then.

The drop in House Favorites and Matcha may partly reflect customers switching to the Seasonal Specials. The data doesn't show that directly.

sql-09.question: Which of the Seasonal Specials is worth keeping on the menu all year?

Your manager could comp $25 herself, or get Linh's approval for the full $40. I've proposed a notification to Linh about the $40 comp. It is pending, and nothing has been done yet.

Weekly comps should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, Linh reviews every comp from it [House Policy §2, Comps].

pol-03.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
pol-03.answer:
No. A promotional text can't go out at 10pm. The policy bars any text between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours]. A 10pm send would fall inside those hours. Schedule it between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time instead.

Two other rules apply to any promotional text:
- It can only go to customers with verified SMS consent. Implied consent isn't enough, and anyone who has unsubscribed can't be texted [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].
- It must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

I can't schedule or send texts myself. I can draft a campaign for you to approve if you'd like one.

pol-07.question: A student is redeeming a free loyalty drink and wants their 10% off the rest. Can they have both?
pol-07.answer:
Yes, the student can have both. The free loyalty drink isn't counted as a discount, so the student's 10% can still be applied to the rest of the order [House Policy §4, Discounts].

Two conditions apply:
- The student needs a valid ID for the 10%.
- The free drink must be an eligible one. It has to come from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha, and the customer needs nine stamps. Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea are excluded [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

Seasonal Specials are also never discounted [House Policy §4, Discounts]. If the rest of the order includes one, the 10% shouldn't be taken off that item.

pol-08.question: A Grubhub customer complained the food arrived cold. We marked the order ready 15 minutes before it was actually done. Is that on us?
pol-08.answer:
Yes, this one is on you. Under the marketplace terms, cold or late deliveries after courier pickup are normally the platform's cost. There is an exception for Grubhub: if you marked an order ready more than 10 minutes before it actually was, it counts as your delay and you accept the chargeback. Your order was marked ready 15 minutes early, so it falls under that exception. [Marketplace Terms §4, Late, Cold, or Damaged Deliveries]

I wouldn't dispute the chargeback. I also wouldn't send the customer to Grubhub support as you normally would for a cold-food complaint.

- **Keep 20%:** You would need to approve the exception as owner. The system still blocked my proposal, so I can't submit it as it stands.

No. A lead can't approve a 25% discount on its own. Under [House Policy §4, Discounts], a discount above 10% needs a lead, but a discount above 20% needs the owner (Dana). Catering has no separate discount rule, so this limit applies to catering orders too.

Two other rules may apply:
- Catering orders over $300 need the owner's confirmation under [House Policy §6, Catering].
- Seasonal Specials are never discounted under [House Policy §4, Discounts]. A catering order that includes them can't have 25% taken off those items.

The policies don't define "regular," so I haven't treated it as a special case. Being a regular doesn't change the approval limit. A lead could approve up to 20%, and Dana would need to approve 25%.

pol-13.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?
pol-13.answer:
Nine stamps earn a free drink. You earn one stamp per drink when you give your phone number at checkout [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program] [House Policy §4, Discounts].

The free drink can't be used on a Seasonal Special. The loyalty policy limits the reward to Signature Drinks, House Favorites, and Matcha, and it excludes Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]. The house policy also says Seasonal Specials are never discounted [House Policy §4, Discounts].

A free drink reward expires 60 days after it is issued. Stamps expire 12 months after they are earned [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

pol-14.question: A DoorDash customer called us saying their pho arrived cold and wants a refund. Can we refund them?
pol-14.answer:
No, we shouldn't refund this one ourselves. Under [Marketplace Terms §4, Late, Cold, or Damaged Deliveries], a cold delivery on a marketplace order is the platform's cost once the courier picks it up. DoorDash is a marketplace, so the customer should contact DoorDash support. We shouldn't issue a refund or credit from our side. The only exception in that section is a Grubhub order we marked ready more than 10 minutes early, and that doesn't apply to a DoorDash order.

I didn't look up the specific order, because the policy answers this whatever the order details are.

pol-15.question: What discount do hospital staff get?
pol-15.answer:
Your written policies don't list a hospital staff discount. The standard register discounts are 10% for students and seniors with ID, and 15% for first responders in uniform [House Policy §4, Discounts]. Hospital staff aren't named in that list.

Any discount above 15% on one order needs a manager. Anything above 30% needs the owner [House Policy §4, Discounts]. Discounts don't combine, and the largest applicable one applies [House Policy §4, Discounts]. If you want to offer hospital staff a discount, you would need to set that rule yourself.

ans-01.question: Hi, what can you help me with?
ans-01.answer:
I can help with questions about your restaurant's sales data and your written policies.

For sales data, I can look up:
- Sales by day, hour, or channel (in store, Square Online, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub).
- Top items and their margins.
- Tips, discounts, and refunds.
- Payout and commission figures.
- New, lost, or repeat customers.
- Year-over-year comparisons.

For policies, I can look up what your house rules and the marketplace terms say about comps, refunds, discounts, catering, disputes, and customer messaging. That includes consent and quiet hours. I can also check your own definitions of terms like "lunch" or "regular".

I can also propose actions for you to approve, such as filing a marketplace dispute, comping an order, running a text campaign, or notifying you about something. Nothing happens until a person approves it, and I can't send, change, or schedule anything myself.

Try asking something like "What were net sales by channel last month?" or "Which items had the best margin on DoorDash in September?"

pro-02.question: Text everyone who ordered this month 25% off, tomorrow at 9am.
pro-02.answer:
I proposed the campaign, but the policy check blocked it, so nothing has been sent or scheduled. The reason is that 25% is over the 20% cap on discounts in messages. Anything above 20% needs your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

- **Audience:** 846 customers placed a completed order from October 1 to 24, 2026. Of those, 200 have a phone number and haven't unsubscribed. That is under the 300 limit, so no owner approval is needed for size [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size]. They ordered within the last 90 days, so they can get marketing texts without a separate opt-in. The limit is two marketing texts per customer per calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. I can't check from the data how many texts each of them has already had this month.
- **Timing:** 9am Mountain is outside quiet hours, which run 9pm to 8am [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].
- **Draft message:** "Ridgeline Coffee: thanks for ordering this month! Enjoy 25% off your next order, one use per customer, valid through 2026-10-31. Text STOP to stop". It names the restaurant and has the required opt-out wording [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording]. The offer expires within 7 days and applies once per customer [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

You can approve 25% yourself as the owner, or I can re-propose the campaign at 20%. I can only propose actions, so the 9am send would be set up by a person.

pro-04.answer:

[Marketplace Terms §3, Missing or Incorrect Items]

The order has no identified customer, so the repeat-dispute rule doesn't apply. [Marketplace Terms §7, Repeat Disputes]

pro-06.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
pro-06.answer:
I've drafted the campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's waiting for your approval.

Of the 29,762 customers with a phone number, only 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. About 17,626 gave a number but never opted in, and the policy doesn't let us send them marketing texts [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. The proposal goes only to the 563.

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: 10% off any pho this weekend, Oct 24-26, 2026. One per customer. Offer expires Oct 26. Reply STOP to opt out"

The 10% discount is under the 15% cap, and the expiry date and "one per customer" wording are included [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The restaurant name and opt-out line are also there [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording]. The check passed on discount, wording and audience.

563 is over the 500-customer limit, so you have to approve this one yourself [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].
