It would go only to customers who have ordered in the last 90 days and have a phone number, or who have verified SMS consent [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. The message would name Ridgeline Coffee and end with "Text STOP to stop" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

- **What I need from you:** Send me the order ID, or the time the ticket was rung in. I can then match it and attach it to the comp request.
- **Weekly cap:** Total comps in a week should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, the owner reviews every comp from it [House Policy §2, Comps].

sql-01.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
sql-01.answer:
Lunch 20 brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than the same dates last year. Net sales here means gross minus discounts minus refunds, for completed in-store and Square Online orders from 11:00 to 13:59 local time, August 3 to 30. That window ran 2026 against 2025 on the same dates, hours and channels [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] [Definitions §2, Lunch].

In 2026 the window had 1,414 orders, $40,261.46 gross, $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 refunded, so $34,610.93 net. In 2025 it had 1,194 orders, $34,989.77 gross, $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 refunded, so $32,859.57 net. The 811 promo orders in 2026 account for most of the extra discounting, which rose by $3,876.05.

Gross sales alone rose by $5,271.69, and gross minus discounts rose by $1,395.64. The $1,751.36 figure is the one that also accounts for refunds.

detail.purpose: Lunch 20 window (Aug 3-30, 11:00-13:59 local, in_store and square_online) vs same dates 2025: completed order count, gross, discounts, net of refunds
detail.sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN created_at >= timestamp '2026-08-03' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants) THEN '2026' ELSE '2025' END AS yr,
  COUNT(*) AS orders,
  SUM(gross_sales_cents) AS gross_cents,
  SUM(discount_cents) AS discount_cents,
  SUM(gross_sales_cents - discount_cents) AS gross_minus_discount_cents,
  SUM(COALESCE((SELECT SUM(p.refunded_amount_cents) FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id),0)) AS refunded_cents,
  SUM(CASE WHEN discount_name ILIKE '%lunch 20%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS promo_orders
FROM orders o
WHERE state = 'completed'
  AND channel IN ('in_store','square_online')
  AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (created_at AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants))) BETWEEN 11 AND 13
  AND (
    (created_at >= timestamp '2026-08-03' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants) AND created_at < timestamp '2026-08-31' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants))
    OR
    (created_at >= timestamp '2025-08-03' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants) AND created_at < timestamp '2025-08-31' AT TIME ZONE (SELECT timezone FROM merchants))
  )
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id

ORDER BY 1

detail.text:
Lunch 20 brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than the same dates last year. Net sales here means gross minus discounts minus refunds, for completed in-store and Square Online orders from 11:00 to 13:59 local time, August 3 to 30. That window ran 2026 against 2025 on the same dates, hours and channels [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] [Definitions §2, Lunch].

In 2026 the window had 1,414 orders, $40,261.46 gross, $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 refunded, so $34,610.93 net. In 2025 it had 1,194 orders, $34,989.77 gross, $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 refunded, so $32,859.57 net. The 811 promo orders in 2026 account for most of the extra discounting, which rose by $3,876.05.

Gross sales alone rose by $5,271.69, and gross minus discounts rose by $1,395.64. The $1,751.36 figure is the one that also accounts for refunds.

sql-03.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
sql-03.answer: You lost 177 regulars over the summer. I used the restaurant's definition: a regular is a customer with three or more completed orders in March, April and May 2026, and a lost regular is one with no completed order since the end of August. Of the 599 customers who were regulars in spring, 177 had no completed order from September 1 through today (2026-10-24). Only 8 of those 177 have verified SMS consent and no unsubscribe, so most can't be reached by text. [Definitions §4, Regulars]

sql-04.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
sql-04.answer:
The side dish that earns the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery is Pickled Vegetables. Across all completed Uber Eats delivery orders to date, it sold 193 units at an average price of $3.11, with food cost of $0.63. After Uber's 30% delivery commission of $0.93, it nets about $1.55 per unit. The next lowest is Fried Egg at about $1.61 per unit. The other sides run from $1.89 (Extra Noodles) up to $3.22 (Extra Meat). These per-unit figures use each item's average marketplace price, and the query did not filter by date.

The 30% rate comes from [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing], and the commission is applied to the order's gross sales as defined in [Definitions §5, Marketplaces].

sql-05.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
sql-05.answer:
In September 2026, the restaurant kept about $2.64 more per order for an in-store sale than for a DoorDash delivery sale. An in-store order averaged $30.11 net, and a DoorDash delivery order averaged $27.47.

These figures cover completed orders dated September 2026 in local time: 2,633 in-store orders and 1,269 DoorDash delivery orders. The in-store figure is the average gross of $32.92, less an average discount of $1.61 and an average processing fee of $1.20. The DoorDash delivery figure is the average gross of $39.35, less an average discount of $2.04, less DoorDash's 25% commission of $9.84 on delivery orders [Marketplace Terms §2, Commission and Pricing]. I used gross sales as a stand-in for the menu subtotal the commission is charged on, and I did not deduct a processing fee for DoorDash because marketplace orders are charged commission instead. DoorDash pickup orders, which carry a 15% commission, were excluded from the delivery comparison.

sql-09.question: Which of the Seasonal Specials is worth keeping on the menu all year?
sql-09.answer:
Maple Pecan Cold Brew is the Seasonal Special worth keeping all year. Under the house definition, the keeper is the special that earned the most total margin over last season (September to December 2025). Maple Pecan Cold Brew earned $7,183.20 of gross margin on 1,460 units and $9,855.00 in revenue, ahead of Peppermint Mocha at $6,644.40, Pumpkin Spice Latte at $6,414.24 and Apple Cider Chai at $6,255.16. The figures cover completed orders from September 1 to December 31, 2025, using the menu price minus food cost, so they are before any marketplace commission, which I did not apply. [Definitions §3, Seasonal Specials]

The specials sell only from September through December. There are no sales from January to August in any year, so this ranking does not show how they would perform off-season. Also, the sales data includes orders dated 2026-10-27, after today's date, which may be a timestamp issue worth checking.

pol-01.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
pol-01.answer: No, not on her own. Under the house comp rule, a manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. Anything above $25 needs the owner, Linh, who can be reached by text during service [House Policy §2, Comps]. A $40 comp would need Linh's approval first. If the complaint is about something other than food quality or wait time, the policies don't cover it. Comps also count toward the weekly limit of 1% of that week's gross sales, and if a week goes over, the owner reviews every comp from that week [House Policy §2, Comps]. The manager can't comp for friends, family, or staff at any amount [House Policy §2, Comps].

pol-02.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on a DoorDash order?
pol-02.answer: Ridgeline Coffee does not list on DoorDash, so there is no DoorDash dispute window for this restaurant. The policy says anyone asking about DoorDash should be told the restaurant is not on any delivery marketplace [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §2, Delivery Marketplaces]. The orders data agrees: all sales come from in-store and Square Online orders, with no DoorDash orders on record. So a DoorDash chargeback you may have seen is either a mistake or something filed under another name, and it's worth checking the card processor or whoever sent the notice. For a missing item on one of your own Square Online pickup orders, the policy covers wrong drinks, which are remade on the spot [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §3, Pickup Orders]. The policies I searched do not set a dispute deadline for any marketplace, because you have none to dispute on.

pol-03.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
pol-03.answer: No, a promotional text can't go out at 10pm. The messaging policy bars any text of any kind between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours], so the earliest permitted time is 9am local. For customers whose local time isn't known, the policy uses Central time. Marketing texts also need verified SMS consent, must end with "Reply STOP to opt out," and must name the restaurant [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts; Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording]. I haven't checked the customer list for this, and I can't schedule or send anything myself. If you want a campaign, I can propose one for approval, and it would need to go out after 9am local time.

pro-02.question: Text everyone who ordered this month 25% off, tomorrow at 9am.
pro-02.answer:
I did not set up the campaign as asked. The proposal was blocked because the house rules cap text discounts at 20% without the owner's approval, and you asked for 25% [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. Nothing has been sent or scheduled, and I cannot schedule a send for 9am tomorrow in any case.

The audience is 214 customers. That is everyone with a completed order in October 2026 who has a phone number on file and has not unsubscribed. Only one of them has verified SMS consent, 55 have implied consent only, and 158 have neither. They can still be texted because they ordered in the last 90 days, which allows up to two marketing texts a month without a separate opt-in [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. The audience is under the 300-customer limit [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size]. I could not check whether any of them have already received two marketing texts this month.

If you want to go ahead, I can propose the same campaign at 20%, which needs no owner approval, or you can approve a 25% offer yourself. Either way, the message must name Ridgeline Coffee, end with "Text STOP to stop," and expire within 7 days [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages; Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording]. Someone would still need to set the send time for 9am.

pro-04.question: File a missing-item dispute with Uber Eats for order 194921.
pro-04.answer:
I haven't filed anything, because this order doesn't meet the dispute rule yet. Order 194921 was an Uber Eats order on 28 September 2026 for $85.95 gross ($94.76 total with tax and tip). The Uber Eats dispute window is 30 days, so it closes on 28 October, which leaves four days. Filing is still within the window.

The problem is the packing photo. Orders over $40 can only be disputed if a packing photo from the pass shows the item in the bag. If no photo exists, the policy says not to dispute and to accept the chargeback as a packing miss [Marketplace Terms §3, Missing or Incorrect Items]. My data does not include photo records, so I can't confirm whether one exists. Please check the pass photo for this order. If it shows the missing item, I can propose the dispute. If it doesn't, the policy says to log it as a packing miss.

The records also don't say which item the customer reported missing. The order has five items: Shrimp Pho, Spring Roll Vermicelli Bowl, Meatball Sandwich, Pork Chop with Shredded Pork and Egg Cake on Rice, and Lemongrass Fried Tofu. The dispute needs that item named. The payment shows no refund recorded on our side (refunded amount $0.00), so the customer refund may have been issued by Uber Eats and not yet reflected here.

pro-06.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
pro-06.answer:
I've proposed the text campaign, but nothing has been sent. It is waiting for your approval.

The audience is 563 customers who gave a phone number and verified SMS consent, and who have not unsubscribed. I left out 17,135 customers who gave a number only with implied consent, since the policy does not allow marketing texts to them [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. I also left out 848 customers who have unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].

The message reads: "Mekong Noodle House: 10% off any pho this weekend. One per customer, valid through Sunday, October 25. Reply STOP to opt out." The 10% discount is within the 15% limit, and the expiry is within 14 days and includes "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The opt-out wording and restaurant name are included [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

Because the audience is over 500, you need to approve it yourself [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size]. The check passed the other items. Pho is on the menu under Noodle Soups, and the catering pho bar and the spice kit are also on the menu. I did not check how many of the 563 have not ordered in 180 days. Any campaign to that group also needs your approval under the same section.

pro-07.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
pro-07.answer:
I can't set up this campaign as you asked. Our messaging policy says Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message, and a discount in a text can't exceed 20% without your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. I haven't proposed anything.

If you want to reach regulars, the policy's existing-relationship rule covers customers who ordered in the last 90 days and gave us a phone number, and they can receive up to two marketing texts a month without a separate opt-in [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. Right now 540 customers fit that group and haven't unsubscribed, as of today. That is more than the 300 a single campaign can reach without your approval, so you would need to sign off on the audience size [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].

I can propose a text to those customers with a discount of up to 20% on items outside Seasonal Specials, expiring within 7 days and usable once per customer, if you tell me the percentage and the items you want included. You would still need to approve the audience size.

pro-08.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
pro-08.answer:
I can't identify table 12's ticket from the data. The orders table has no table field, so I can't tell which order that was. Today has about 40 completed or near-$60 orders, and several in-store ones could fit, but I won't guess and comp the wrong one. If you send me the order number, I can check it and prepare the comp.

Policy also matters here. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a food quality complaint, and anything above $25 needs the owner's approval [House Policy §2, Comps]. A $60 comp is above that limit, so it would need your sign-off. Once you give me the order, I can propose the comp for your approval.
